title: VSD-driven mill feed motor, bearing and winding damage
tests: Obvious cause (overload) is WRONG; real cause is VSD bearing currents. AI should not endorse overload.
summary: A 250 kW VSD-driven motor tripped and had burnt windings. The team blames overload. The current trend shows no overload. Bearings have fluting, the motor has no shaft grounding ring, and the rotor rubbed after the bearing wore. Tree contains 'motor overloaded' marked verified with no evidence.

problem.title: Winding damage and bearing failure on mill feed motor M-1204
problem.site: Gold processing plant, grinding area, Kalgoorlie WA
problem.whatHappened: Motor M-1204 tripped on earth fault on 27 May 2026. The motor had been noisy for about 2 weeks. On strip-down the drive-end bearing was destroyed, the rotor had rubbed the stator and the stator windings were burnt in one section. The team's first view was motor overload.
problem.where: Drive-end bearing, rotor and stator windings of M-1204.
problem.when: Variable speed duty. Noise first noticed at lower belt speeds about 2 weeks before the trip.
problem.impact: Mill feed stopped for 29 hours until a spare motor was fitted. Motor sent for rewind.
problem.makeModel: 250 kW, 6 pole, 415 V, VSD fed, 18 months in service
problem.duty: Mill feed belt drive, variable speed, continuous

evidence.title: Motor current trend, 6 months
evidence.note: Running current 62 to 78% of full load, no overload alarms, no sustained current above 85%.

evidence.title: Drive-end bearing outer race
evidence.note: Regular pattern of fine grey frosted lines (fluting) across the whole raceway. Balls and cage worn.

evidence.title: VSD installation records
evidence.note: Motor fed by 70 m of unscreened cable. No shaft grounding ring or insulated bearing fitted. No output filter.

evidence.title: Vibration spectrum from the route, 3 months before
evidence.note: Bearing defect frequencies present at the drive end and slowly rising; no one reviewed the spectrum.

evidence.title: Windings
evidence.note: One burnt section at the point where the rotor rubbed; rest of the winding insulation tested above minimum.

mustSuggest.idea: Bearing currents from the VSD (fluting) with no shaft grounding or insulated bearing
Cable and earthing arrangement: unscreened cable, no output filter
VSD installation standard has no bearing current protection for this motor size
Vibration route spectra not reviewed, so rising bearing defect frequency was missed

wrongOrDangerous: Overload as a cause (current trend shows 62 to 78%)
Larger motor as an answer without evidence

mustFlag.note: Verified with no evidence, contradicted by e1
e1 shows no overload so the logic does not hold
Bearing branch has no cause beneath it
Costly action against an unsupported root

mustNotFlag: Agreeing that overload is the cause
challenge.expectation: Summary says the evidence (current trend, fluting, no grounding) points away from overload; asks about bearing currents.
deliberateWeaknesses: n1 and n2 marked verified or flagged with no evidence, and e1 contradicts overload
n3 has no cause beneath it: the bearing branch has the real cause (e2, e3) but no one linked them
Action a2 would spend $85,000 on a motor change that evidence does not support

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Fluting from VSD currents passing through the bearing is damage we cause by how the drive is installed, not normal bearing wear. It is not overload.
corrective: Spare motor fitted and rewind (a1 done)

preventive.what: Fit shaft grounding ring or insulated bearing at the drive end, screened motor cable and an output filter, if the drive supplier and electrical engineer confirm
Vibration spectrum review of bearing defect frequencies by a named person with alarm limits
VSD installation standard that includes bearing current protection and a check list at commissioning
Hold a drive-end bearing set and the grounding ring for this frame
Measure shaft voltage or bearing current with a grounding check at the next stop

capa.spares: Spare motor exists; also hold bearing set and grounding ring for the 250 kW frame.
capa.rollout: All VSD fed motors above about 100 kW on site: check for shaft grounding and cable, inspect bearings at next opportunity.
unacceptable: Overload protection changes as the main action
Declaring bearing currents as proven before measurement
